The Bosch Group
Pioneering Tomorrow with 
Innovation and Impact
The Bosch Group is a 
global technology and services company with over 417,900 associates worldwide as of December 31, 2024. In 2024, it reported sales of 90.3 billion euros. Bosch operates across four key sectors: Mobility, Industrial Technology, Consumer Goods, and Energy and Building Technology.
Innovation lies at the core of 
Bosch’s progress. With 136 R&D locations and nearly 86,800 associates in research and development, including close to 48,000 software professionals, the Group is shaping solutions for both today and the future.
2
=== page 6 ===
Guided by long-term trends such 
as automation, electrification, digitalization, and sustainability, the Bosch Group continues to evolve. Its diversified presence enables agility and drives innovation across industries.
The Group leverages its strengths 
in sensors, software, and services to deliver integrated solutions that enhance convenience, efficiency, and safety. With the growing role of connectivity and artificial intelligence, Bosch is developing technologies that are both intuitive and resource efficient. This aligns with its purpose, ‘Invented for life.’
The Bosch Group comprises Robert 
Bosch GmbH and approximately 490 subsidiaries and regional companies in more than 60 countries. Supported by a global network of manufacturing, engineering, and sales operations, along with trusted partners, it reaches customers in nearly every market.
Innovation lies at the core of 
Bosch’s progress. With 136 R&D locations and nearly 86,800 associates in research and development, including close to 48,000 software professionals, the Group is shaping solutions for both today and the future.
Founded in Stuttgart in 1886 by 
Robert Bosch, the Group is guided by a distinctive ownership structure that ensures long-term focus. Ninety-four percent of Robert Bosch GmbH’s share capital is held by the charitable Robert Bosch Stiftung GmbH. The remaining shares are held by the company and a Bosch family-owned entity. Strategic direction is provided by Robert Bosch Industrietreuhand KG.
For Bosch in India, this global 
foundation enables local innovation, agile responses to market dynamics, and meaningful contributions to industry and society.Financial Highlights

Bosch India
Nurturing Innovation 
through Diverse Expertise
As an integral part of the global Bosch Group, Bosch India 
(referred to as ‘Bosch India Limited,’ ‘Bosch Limited,’ ‘Bosch,’ ‘our Company,’ or ‘we’) plays a pivotal role in driving innovation, advancing engineering, and delivering integrated technology solutions across sectors. India hosts the Group’s largest development center outside Germany, offering end-to-end capabilities across software, electronics, and mechanical domains. This center plays a critical role in supporting Bosch’s global growth strategy and technological leadership.
4
=== page 8 ===
We operate through a network 
of 15 companies that blend the precision of German engineering with the agility, scale, and talent of India. Our entities include Bosch Limited (our flagship listed company), Bosch Chassis Systems India Private Limited, Bosch Rexroth (India) Private Limited, Bosch Global Software Technologies Private Limited, Bosch Automotive Electronics India Private Limited, Bosch Electrical Drives India Private Limited, BSH Home Appliances Private Limited, ETAS Automotive India Private Limited, Robert Bosch Automotive Steering Private Limited, Automobility Services and Solutions Private Limited, Newtech Filter India Private Limited, Precision Seals Manufacturing Limited, Robert Bosch India Manufacturing and Technology Private Limited, MICO Trading Private Limited, and Mivin Engineering Technologies Private Limited.
Since commencing operations in 
1951, we have steadily expanded our footprint across 17 manufacturing sites and 7 development and application centers, supporting both domestic and global markets. These facilities enable us to localize solutions, drive innovation, and respond with speed to dynamic customer and industry requirements.
In FY 2024–25, we reported net 
revenue of ` 373,457 million 
(approximately euros 4.13 billion) and employed 38,655 associates as of March 31, 2025.
Bosch Limited continues to anchor 
the Group’s India presence with a sharp focus on next-generation mobility, smart manufacturing, and digital transformation.

Chairman’s Message
Designing 
What’s Next with Purpose and Precision Dear Shareholders,
The year 2024-25 has been a year 
of global uncertainty and has been a challenging year both abroad and in India. Yet I connect once again with you with a sense of humility and satisfaction at the closure for Bosch Limited’s journey in FY 2024–25. It was not merely about steering through headwinds in the year gone by, it was about embracing change with purpose, strengthening our foundations, and setting the pace for the future and securing a good result for the year.
This year’s theme, “Navigating the 
New; Building the Next”, is the lens through which we are continuously evolving and reimagining value creation in a rapidly transforming India and world.
14
=== page 18 ===
Resilience in a Reshaped World
2024 was a year of shifting paradigms. Across the globe, economic recovery faced challenges from persistent 
geopolitical tensions, elevated inflation, and evolving trade routes. India, in contrast, retained its title as one of the fastest-growing major economies. More than macro indicators, what stands out is the quality of growth: formalized, digitized, and aspirational. We need this sustained growth for us to be able to realize our dream of a “Viksit” India.
At Bosch Limited, we view these shifts not as disruptions, but as catalysts. The opportunities in sustainable 
mobility, digitization, and advanced manufacturing are vast, and we are aligning ourselves to be ahead of the curve.
Engaging Stakeholders and Creating Shared Value
Bosch’s success is rooted in our deep and sustained engagement with all stakeholders. 
With society, we take 
pride in advancing 
our legacy of skill 
development, reaching 
a significant milestone 
of training over 100,000 
youth with essential 
skills, paving the way 
for dignified livelihoods 
and fostering inclusive 
growth. Guided by 
Bosch’s expertise and 
driven by our vision, 
this year we added 
yet another social 
engagement focus of 
“sustainable mobility” 
aimed at fostering a 
cleaner, safer world. 
We also continued to 
invest in education, 
supporting schools 
and Anganwadis (early 
childhood care and 
education centers) to 
create nurturing spaces 
for holistic learning. In 
healthcare, our Mobile 
Medical Units and 
clean drinking water 
initiatives prioritized 
community wellness at 
the grassroots levelWith governments, 
both central and 
state, we are actively 
participating in 
India’s industrial 
growth through policy 
advocacy around 
future technologies, 
manufacturing and 
green technologies. 
We have continued 
to take feedback 
from shareholders, 
investors and analysts 
alike to further push 
ourselves in the path of 
consistent growth. With our suppliers, 
our investments in 
supply chain digitization 
and localization have 
enhanced resilience, 
even during volatile 
times. Our high 
localization rate (more 
than 90% in traditional 
business) reinforces 
national value chains in 
line with the “Make in 
India” initiative. With our suppliers, 
our investments in

and localization have

Strategic 
Evolution: From Hardware to Intelligence
Bosch Limited has expertise 
not just in manufacturing, we are a technology partner in transformation. The mobility ecosystem is shifting from hardware-driven engineering to software-defined experiences. We are responding by strengthening and further enhancing our capabilities in embedded systems, safety solutions, and energy transition technologies.
Our focus on electrification, 
hydrogen-based mobility, and AI-powered platforms is preparing us for long-term relevance in a fast-digitizing market.
Sustainability: A 
Non-Negotiable Compass
ESG continues to be central to our 
strategy in creating differentiated value to our customers. Bosch Limited currently leads the world in terms of global auto component companies achieving the lowest risk ratings. We are driven by strong performance across energy conservation, emissions reduction, and operational governance including circular economy initiatives to reduce waste and improve recyclability across product lifecycles keeping customer centricity as a focus area.Our People: The 
Foundation of All Progress
As we grow technologically, we 
remain deeply human-centric. We are proud of the culture we’ve built, of empowerment, capability, and inclusivity. From leadership development to continuous learning in AI and analytics, our teams are future-ready because we invest in their readiness. Our people are our greatest assets and our collective energy and commitment have helped us turn challenges into chapters of progress.
Looking Ahead: 
Leadership with Purpose
As we continue to race into the 
future, we see an India that is building its place in global value chains, not just as a market, but as an innovation and manufacturing powerhouse.

MD’s Message
Creating 
Impact with Agility and Commitment Dear Shareholders,
It gives me intense pleasure to 
present to you the Annual Report of Bosch Limited for the fiscal year 2024–25. As I reflect on the past year, I feel a deep sense of pride, not only in our performance but also in the resilience, innovation, and agility shown by our teams.
In a world shaped by economic 
uncertainty and complex global dynamics, Bosch Limited has continued to move forward with purpose, staying rooted in its values and adapting quickly to meet the moment.
Global Economic 
Environment
The global economic landscape in 
2024 was shaped by a series of
interlinked challenges. Geopolitical 
tensions, especially in Ukraine and the Middle East have continued
to affect global stability and trade 
flows. Supply chain disruptions and inflationary headwinds persisted across regions, dampening business confidence and raising input costs in many sectors.
Guruprasad 
Mudlapur
Managing Director, Bosch 
Limited
18
=== page 22 ===
Despite these challenges, Bosch 
Group demonstrated remarkable strength and adaptability. We concluded the fiscal year with sales revenue of €90.3 billion,  a 
reflection of our consistent drive towards excellence. Our Strategy 
2030 , anchored on sustainability, 
digital transformation, and long- term value creation is enabling us to stay competitive in a world where innovation cycles are
shorter, and customer expectations 
are evolving faster than ever. We are focused on building structural resilience while preparing for emerging market shifts.
India: Growth Amid 
Global Volatility
Closer to home, India continued to 
present one of the most promising economic outlooks globally. The post-pandemic resurgence is no longer a rebound, it’s a transformation. Strategic
investments in infrastructure, rapid 
digitization, and rising consumer confidence have fueled steady growth.
According to the IMF’s World 
Economic Outlook (April 2025 edition), India is projected to grow at 6.2% in 2025 and 6.3% in 2026, making it one of the fastest- growing major economies globally. These numbers reflect more than just economic performance, they speak to the nation’s long-term structural strengths: a young demographic, expanding digital access, and growing aspirations.
For Bosch Limited, this 
macroeconomic environment is rich with opportunity. Our growing presence in mobility, consumer goods, industrial technology, and digital services puts us in a strong position to contribute to and benefit from India’s continued rise.
Bosch Limited: Performance Highlights
In FY 2024–25, Bosch Limited delivered revenue from operations of INR 18,087 crores, a growth of 8.1% over the previous year. This growth reflects a balanced contribution across segments and is especially commendable considering the wider global and local headwinds.
In the Mobility Business 
Sector, we recorded 
a 7.0% increase in 
product sales, led by 
robust demand in the 
2-wheeler segment, 
passenger vehicle and 
tractor segments. Our 
overall domestic sales 
grew by 6.2%.The Powertrain 
Solutions division saw a 
5.8% increase in sales, 
benefiting from strong 
tractor demand and 
increase in content per 
vehicle.
The Mobility 
Aftermarket division 
grew by 8.4%, driven 
by increased market 
demand for diesel 
components and filters.Our Beyond Mobility 
sector registered a 4.4% 
rise, due to improved 
sales in the consumer 
goods segment.
In recognition of these strong results, the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR 512 per share for FY 2024–25. As a continued portfolio action, Bosch Limited divested its 6.97% stake in Nivaata Systems Pvt. Ltd. (Routematic). This investment, initiated in 2020 to explore digital office commute solutions, achieved its strategic objectives, and we exit with valuable learnings and experience.

ANNUAL REPORT 2024-25 
=== page 23 ===
Strategic Direction 
and Future Focus
At Bosch, innovation isn’t a 
buzzword, it’s a way of working. We continued to invest in local R&D in mobility and beyond mobility segments, launching products tailored for the Indian market, such as AVENAR fire detectors and IP cameras developed and produced in India. These efforts reinforce our commitment to the ‘Make in India’ mission and help enhance self-reliance in high-tech manufacturing.
Looking ahead, we are doubling 
down on sustainable mobility. Our portfolio is expanding to include hydrogen-based technologies, electric vehicle solutions, and digitally enabled services. These will position us as a key player in the global push for decarbonization, while serving evolving customer expectations in India and beyond.
Digital transformation is also 
a cornerstone of our strategy. Whether through smarter supply chains, predictive maintenance, or customer experience tools, Bosch is embedding digital technologies to reimagine the way we work and deliver value.
Manufacturing 
Excellence: Built in India, Built for the World
Our India Operations Strategy, 
focused on Customer Centricity, Innovative Industrialization, Operational Excellence, and People Development has powered strong progress this year. We have been recognized with 15 customer awards, including for Overall Performance, Zero Defects, and Customer Centricity. In 2024, we achieved the lowest risk rating globally (5.9 among 245 global automotive companies), a testament to our focus on sustainability, resource conservation, and climate action.
We expanded capacity with 
projects like the NOx line at our Bidadi plant and diversification of our Power Tools portfolio in Chennai. Our localization rate now stands at 91% for conventional businesses and 53% for new-generation products, demonstrating our commitment to strengthening local value chains. Through over 100 digital projects across our plants, we’ve leveraged AI and data analytics to improve quality, reduce downtime, and enhance productivity ranging from automated visual inspection systems to predictive analytics in production lines.
Sustainability, 
CSR, and Innovation
Sustainability is a core part 
of our DNA. We are proud of the progress we have made on the Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) front. From energy conservation to circularity practices, Bosch is walking the talk on sustainability.
Our Corporate Social 
Responsibility (CSR) initiatives continue to create lasting impact in education, healthcare, skilling, and environmental protection. These efforts aren’t simply about compliance, they are about creating inclusive growth and shared value.
These collective efforts were 
recognized through the Golden Peacock Award, the Avtar & Seramount Award, and the Karma Award, all of which affirm our unwavering commitment to creating a sustainable, scalable impact.
We have also been recognized 
amongst the Top 20 most innovative companies in India by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), a significant rise
from our previous Top 50 position. 
This underscores our commitment 
20
=== page 24 ===
to nurturing a culture of innovation 
across the board.
Our continued engagement with 
industry bodies and associations such as CII, ACMA, SIAM and others have ensured that we continue to engage in policy advocacy in our areas of operation.
Gratitude and the

Innovative 
Solutions for Enhanced Performance Connectivity
The construction industry is 
undergoing a rapid transformation with the rise of automation, prefabrication, and digitally enabled workflows. These shifts are helping streamline operations, reduce on-site labor and equipment dependency, and create new opportunities to enhance user productivity and comfort. At Bosch, we’re helping lead this shift by delivering smart technologies that raise performance standards and make jobsites more efficient.
Vibration Control 
Prolonged exposure to high levels of vibration can result in fatigue, decreased productivity, and, in severe cases, Hand Arm Vibration Syndrome (HAVS), commonly known as Vibration White Finger. Our Vibration Control Side Handle designed to reduce vibration transmission and improve user comfort and control, addressing the above concerns.
Dust Solution 
A clean work environment is essential for precision and performance. Bosch’s integrated Dust Extraction System connects seamlessly with our power tools to minimize dust accumulation, protect user health, and extend the life of tools and accessories. It enables faster, safer work, especially in demanding job site conditions.
Biturbo
Biturbo tools combine high-torque brushless motors with ProCORE18V battery technology to deliver superior cordless performance. These tools are purpose-built for demanding applications, enabling professionals to tackle heavy-duty tasks with greater ease and efficiency.
Cyclon Technology
Our Cyclon Technology eliminates up to 90% of cooling air dust, protecting internal components and significantly extending motor lifespan. This is particularly advantageous in harsh environments with high 
FINANCIAL STATEMENTS ESG STATUTORY REPORTS NOTICE BUSINESS OVERVIEW COMPANY OVERVIEW
41
ANNUAL REPORT 2024-25 
=== page 45 ===
dust exposure, ensuring long-term 
durability and consistent tool performance.
One Chuck 
Bosch’s One Chuck system is designed for versatility and convenience. It accommodates SDS-plus, cylindrical, and hex drill bits, eliminating the need for additional adapters and reducing downtime. The integrated design ensures more precise results without the risk of losing external components.
Kickback Control
Built-in smart sensors continuously monitor tool movement. In the event of sudden and unexpected rotation around the drilling axis, the tool automatically shuts off momentarily and activates a flashing HMI light alerting the user and helping prevent injury. This serves as an added safeguard alongside the standard mechanical safety clutch.
Cool pack Technology
Bosch’s CoolPack technology is a state-of-the-art thermal management system designed to keep lithium-ion batteries cooler during operation. By efficiently dissipating heat, it ensures consistent performance and significantly extends battery life, especially under high workloads.
Tabless Technology
The next-generation ProCORE18V+ battery leverages tabless cell technology, reducing internal resistance by 50%. This enables faster energy flow and lower heat generation, resulting in up to 71% longer runtime and 
enhanced durability. Combined with CoolPack 2.0, it delivers unmatched cordless performance in a compact, efficient form.

=== page 46 ===
Power Tools 
Manufacturing Plant, Chennai (Tamil Nadu)
Our Power Tools manufacturing 
facility in Oragadam, Tamil Nadu, plays a vital role in supporting both domestic and global operations. Spanning approximately 7,000 square meters within the SIPCOT Industrial Growth Center, the plant has been recognized, effective April 1, 2024, as an independent region under Bosch’s global strategy. This development enables the facility to manage production volumes not only for India but also for SAARC countries and Rest of the World (RoW) markets.As India’s leading Power Tools manufacturing unit, the Chennai plant produces a diverse range of equipment, including Small and Large Angle Grinders, Marble Cutters, Blowers, Drills, and Two-Kilogram Hammers, along with their motors. It also serves as the global supply source for Blowers. The facility has achieved a local component share of over 70 percent and a product localization rate exceeding 74 percent. Thus, supporting Bosch’s commitment to building local capabilities.
A notable feature of the plant is 
its fully women-led shopfloor, which reflects Bosch’s approach to inclusive and socially responsible manufacturing. The facility holds ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 certifications and has attained carbon neutrality through a combination of in-house solar energy and green energy procurement. In 2024, the plant achieved its highest production volume to date, manufacturing over 2 million tools.
To further drive innovation and 
competitiveness, Bosch established the India Engineering Center at the site in June 2023. The team focuses on the development of corded tools and deeper localization of components. The center also contributes to the digital transformation of core operations, enhancing efficiency, scalability, and long-term resilience. These initiatives align with the ‘Make in India’ vision and are designed to prepare the plant for future-ready manufacturing.

Climate Action
Bosch wants to make a 
contribution to climate action, an aspiration it has anchored in its sustainability vision. We support the United Nations 2015 Paris Agreement on climate action and the goal formulated therein of limiting global warming to as close to 1.5 degrees Celsius as possible. With carbon neutrality (scope 1 & 2)*, we are making a measurable contribution to this goal.
* Scopes 1, 2, and 3 are used here in 
accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard. We have taken into account the effects of CO₂ and of other greenhouse gases, as well as climate-relevant substances, to the extent that these are of relevance for the analysis. To enable comparability between the climate impact of the various greenhouse gases and substances of relevance for the climate, emissions are presented in CO₂ equivalents. For ease of reading, we use the terms CO₂ and CO₂ equivalents synonymously.
As early as 2020, the Bosch Group 
with its more than 450 locations worldwide has been carbon neutral overall (scope 1 & 2). Four levers were used to achieve carbon neutrality: increasing energy efficiency, generating our own energy from renewable sources (new clean power), purchasing 
electricity from renewable sources (green electricity), and – as the last resort – using carbon credits to offset residual CO₂ emissions.
We are committed to advancing 
renewable energy generation and promoting sustainability through a combination of in-house initiatives and strategic partnerships. This includes generating renewable energy at our own facilities and entering into long-term supply agreements to support the development of new photovoltaic plants. We are also conducting trials with 5 percent ethanol-blended diesel as part of our exploration of more sustainable fuel alternatives.
A key area of focus is the phased 
elimination of high Global Warming Potential (GWP) substances by transitioning to lower-GWP alternatives, thereby reducing our climate footprint.
To systematically manage energy 
efficiency, Bosch Limited has adopted the 4E approach: Energy Audit, Energy Re-tuning, Energy Lifecycle, and Energy Culture. In parallel, we are embracing digital transformation in energy management through the 4C framework: Connect, Communicate, Consolidate, and Cognitive to enable real-time visibility and data-driven decision-making.
In FY 2024–25, 18.6 percent of 
Bosch Limited’s total electricity demand was met through in-house solar power plants.  The volume of purchased green electricity from new plants (PPA) and I-RECs 
To systematically

At the same time, we also want 
to reduce emissions produced outside Bosch’s direct sphere of influence (scope 3), for example at suppliers, in logistics, or when our products are used. Our aim is to reduce these upstream and downstream emissions by 30 percent in absolute terms by 2030, compared with the baseline year 2018 – irrespective of our company’s growth.
Bosch requires water for cooling 
systems, sanitary facilities and technical processes. We are focusing on process improvements, recycling, and the use of rainwater to further reduce water withdrawal at our company locations. In regions with strained water supplies, water is already reused or rainwater is used wherever possible. To ensure that the funds for achieving water targets are used efficiently, water coordinators in the divisions identify local savings potential and implement suitable measures together with those responsible at the sites concerned.
Work safety
Measures to protect and promote associates’ health and provide a safe working environment at all times are a top priority for Bosch. Internal company regulations define the relevant principles, organization and responsibilities within the Bosch Group.
Every year, Bosch Group identifies 
and assess potential occupational safety risks and classify them by priority. For this purpose, we 
refer to accidents reported in the Incident Management System and use findings from internal audits under ISO 45001 or the audits of the internal audit department. On this basis, we develop specific risk mitigation programs and define the focal points for subsequent audits. We carry out an in-depth analysis of any work-related accidents causing at least one day of downtime, irrespective of whether Bosch associates or third-party staff are involved. In the event of serious accidents, special analysis methods are used to perform a detailed investigation of the root causes and to derive specific measures. Based on internal regulations, workplace or activity-related hazard assessments are also carried out regularly. These are used as a basis for determining any preventive and protective measures needed, and our associates are instructed accordingly.

Sustainability Roadmap
Driving Long-term Value 
through Responsible Action
To us, sustainability means 
striking a balance between the economic, environmental, and social dimensions of our business activities as part of responsible corporate governance.
Defined as a group-wide task 
within the Bosch Group, the business sectors pursue the jointly set goals on the basis of systematic sustainability management. The contents, tasks, and related controlling are anchored in the company’s processes. Internal company regulations define the organization and responsibilities for sustainability and EHS in the Bosch Group.
At Bosch Group, the highest 
technical committee for sustainability is the corporate sustainability board (CSB) under the aegis of the chairman of the board of management of Robert Bosch GmbH and the board of management member responsible for sustainability.  
Our Sustainability 
Strategy
 We are convinced that 
sustainability can make a significant contribution to Bosch achieving its growth objectives. Our vision for sustainability with its six dimensions defines the strategic focal points in this respect. Each of these is specified and continually enhanced by reference to two focus activities, where appropriate,

Climate Action
Bosch wants to make a contribution

We support the United Nations 2015 Paris Agreement on climate action and the goal formulated therein of limiting global warming to as close to 1.5 degrees Celsius as possible. *Scopes 1, 2, and 3 are used here in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting 
Standard. We have taken into account the effects of CO₂ and of other greenhouse gases, as well as climate-relevant substances, to the extent that these are of relevance for the analysis. To enable comparability between the climate impact of the various greenhouse gases and substances of relevance for the climate, emissions are presented in CO₂ equivalents. For ease of reading, we use the terms CO₂ and CO₂ equivalents synonymously.
As early as 2020, the Bosch Group 
with its more than 450 locations worldwide has been carbon neutral overall (scope 1 & 2). Four levers were used to achieve carbon neutrality: increasing energy efficiency, generating our own energy from renewable sources (new clean power), purchasing electricity from renewable sources (green electricity), and – as the last resort – using carbon credits to offset residual CO₂ emissions.  * The following applies to information on the Environment management systems: 
production locations and development locations (with material responsibility) with more than 50 associates and that have been included in the consolidated group for more than three years.

 Story Spotlight
Smart Cooling at Nashik
At the Bosch Nashik plant, a groundbreaking initiative titled “Chillers 
Reimagined” is revolutionizing the operation of industrial cooling systems. Traditionally, chillers run on fixed temperature set points, often resulting in excess energy consumption. To improve this, Bosch implemented an artificial intelligence-based system that recalibrates chiller settings every 10 minutes based on real-time performance data.
The system leverages advanced algorithms to predict energy demand, 
fine-tune operational parameters, and maximize cooling efficiency. In addition to significantly reducing energy usage, the solution enables predictive maintenance by identifying potential equipment issues early, thereby minimizing downtime and improving reliability.
Chillers Reimagined demonstrates how digital innovation can 
address legacy inefficiencies while advancing sustainability goals. It exemplifies Bosch’s commitment to smart manufacturing, resource optimization, and climate-conscious operations.At the same time, we also want to reduce emissions produced outside Bosch’s direct sphere of influence (scope 3), for example at suppliers, in logistics, or when our products are used. Our aim is to reduce these upstream and downstream emissions by 30 percent in absolute terms by 2030, compared with the baseline year 2018 – irrespective of our company’s growth. 
The Science Based Targets 
initiative (SBTi) has endorsed our climate targets for the 1.5 degree pathway.# This means that Bosch has science-based climate targets for the entire value chain – from purchasing to the product use phase. Our targets are based on an internal analysis of potential, which we have compared with SBTi’s cross-sector ambition.
#Robert Bosch GmbH’s entry in the

Water
Responsible Water Use: 
Conserving Every Drop
Conscientious use of water is 
a major priority for Bosch. We especially focus on counteracting the increasing scarcity of water. The Bosch Group has set a target of reducing absolute water withdrawal at 70 sites in regions with water scarcity by 25 percent by 2025 compared with 2017 baseline year.  The sites were identified using the Water Risk Filter of the World Wildlife Fund for Nature.
At Bosch Limited, six out of our 
seven locations are situated in water-stressed regions, underscoring the importance of our water conservation efforts.Turning Heat into Energy
As part of its ongoing energy innovation efforts, the Bosch Nashik plant has implemented a project titled “Efficient Energy Recovery” that captures and repurposes waste heat from compressors. Instead of allowing this heat to dissipate, the system redirects it to meet internal heating requirements through an integrated setup featuring heat exchangers and thermal storage solutions.
This simple yet impactful intervention has resulted in a 40 percent reduction in chiller load and annual 
energy savings of 178 megawatt-hours. By converting waste heat into usable energy, the project exemplifies our approach to practical sustainability that delivers tangible, measurable outcomes.
 Award Spotlight
The Bosch Nashik plant received the ISHRAE Decarbonization Award  from the Indian Society of Heating, 
Refrigerating and Air Conditioning Engineers. This recognition honors our proactive approach to reducing carbon emissions through smart technologies and integrated sustainability strategies. The award highlights Bosch’s continued efforts in climate action, circular resource use, and water stewardship.

Collection systems for 
monsoon rains
A new rainwater collection system 
was put into operation in Bidadi in India in 2023, which has a storage capacity of 10,000 m³. In 2024, around 64,000 m³ of rainwater was collected and used at the site. This covered roughly 41 percent of the total volume of water needed at the site. Rainwater is also used at the site in Naganathapura in India. Around 11,200 m³ of rainwater was treated and used at the plants in 2024, covering roughly 26 percent of the total water demand at the site in this period. 
Across Bosch Limited, rainwater 
harvesting increased by 31.75 percent in 2024–25 compared to the previous year. In total, 90,141.96 cubic meters of rainwater was collected and utilized, covering 16 percent of the company’s overall water demand.
Comprehensive data on water 
withdrawal and usage for 2024–25 is available in the Bosch Sustainability Report section of the Annual Report.Circular Economy: 
Building Loops That Drive Sustainability
With our circular economy 
strategy, we want to enhance the sustainability of our products over their entire life cycle – from procurement and production to use, return, and remanufacturing, right through to recycling and reuse of materials. To this end, we endeavor to either create loops directly within Bosch or close them outside the company using established recycling processes. This way, we reduce the amount of materials used and our products’ carbon footprint* and contribute toward achieving our scope 3 target. At the same time, we also avoid potential risks relating to compliance with environmental and social standards. Building a closed-loop system for materials has the 
*Unless otherwise stated, carbon footprint takes into account all greenhouse gas emissions 
ranging from raw materials extraction to transport, production, sales, and use through to disposal of the product (cradle to grave) (see DIN EN ISO 14067). We aim to establish 
closed material loops, either internally at Bosch or in collaboration with external recycling partners, to maximize the useful life of resources.particular advantage of eliminating 
parts of the value chain that are subject to risks, such as extraction of raw materials. 
This approach reduces raw 
material consumption, lowers our products’ overall carbon footprint* and advances our Scope 3 emissions reduction targets. At the same time, it helps mitigate environmental and social compliance risks linked to raw material extraction. By closing material loops, we avoid the most exposed stages of the value chain and build greater resilience into our operations. Story Spotlight
A Calculated Response to Water Scarcity
Located in Tirunelveli, one of India’s most water-stressed districts, the Bosch Gangaikondan plant adopted a data-driven approach to water conservation. The team conducted a technical survey using ten years of rainfall data to assess the site’s rainwater harvesting potential.
Targeting an annual rainwater capture of 2,000 cubic meters, the site 
initiated a phased implementation plan. This began with a 500 cubic meter collection pond, followed by a 1,000 cubic meter system. With the harvesting pond now operational, the plant is projected to reduce freshwater withdrawal by approximately 1,500 cubic meters each year.
This initiative reflects our commitment to addressing local 
environmental challenges through targeted infrastructure and supports our broader goal of long-term sustainability.

use a model comprising levers that can be applied across the entire value chain (see graphic). Waste: Prioritizing 
Reduction, Recovery, and Responsible Disposal
The previously discussed 
instruments are also relevant for our own activities. This is especially the case with waste management. “Avoid, then reuse, then dispose” – that is the principle we apply at Bosch with respect to waste management. As part of its circular economy strategy, Bosch continues to work systematically on reducing waste volume and, in particular, on recycling. A group guideline defines processes and ensures that the legal requirements for the transport and disposal of waste are complied with locally. All production locations have a clearly designated organizational unit responsible for sorting, classifying, and handing over waste to disposal companies. 
In 2019, we decided to pursue 
two priorities: reducing hazardous waste and minimizing the amount of waste going to landfills. Specific measures are being implemented at sites with relatively large quantities of waste to reduce the amount of waste. Transforming Waste into Value with 
LTO Filtration
At the Jaipur plant, the Nozzle Holder Assembly line 
faced challenges with White Leakage Testing Oil (LTO) turning non-transparent after repeated use, necessitating frequent replacement and generating hazardous waste. To address this, the team implemented a low-cost multimedia filtration process that restores oil clarity and quality, enabling up to 40 percent of LTO to be reused. This solution has significantly reduced fresh-oil consumption and cut waste generation.
Beyond environmental gains, this initiative, cost-
effective improvement earned the Best Kaizen (Environment) Gold Category Award from the Confederation of Indian Industry, showcasing Jaipur’s leadership in sustainable innovation. Story Spotlight
Oil Reclamation and Smart Monitoring 
in Action
At our Bidadi plant, we have implemented a robust 
oil reclamation process that reduces fresh-oil intake and slashes waste generation. This initiative enabled annual fluid savings of 198 kiloliters, underscoring our commitment to environmental stewardship.
The project features an integrated Coolant, Oil, Lube, 
and Chips Management system with real-time digital monitoring and predictive maintenance capabilities. This technology not only enhances operational safety but also boosts efficiency by reducing downtime and optimizing resource utilization.
Use of substances of 
concern
At Bosch Group, substances of 
concern (SoC) are all substances in production aids or products that could have a negative impact on human health or the environment. These include, for example, substances that are classified accordingly or are regulated by law, customer agreements or in-house requirements. Internal company regulations define the material compliance requirements and specify the organization and responsibilities. We are continuously working to identify permissible SoC in our products and processes, adopt substitutes, and reduce or altogether avoid hazardous substances in the long term wherever possible. For example, where technically feasible, we intend to dispense with substances on the EU’s REACH candidate list in new developments. Our internal Design for Environment standard defines the requirements for handling SoC in the product development process. If permissible SoC are unavoidable in the production process for technical reasons, we conduct hazard assessments to ensure suitable protective measures are taken for safe handling of such substances.

Taking Accountability Beyond the Product Lifecycle
Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) is a regulatory framework that requires manufacturers and brand owners 
to manage the environmental impact of their products throughout their entire lifecycles, including post-consumer collection, recycling, and safe disposal.
At Bosch Limited, EPR is not just a legal obligation; it is a strategic opportunity to advance our sustainability 
goals. By actively participating in EPR compliance, we support India’s environmental regulations, promote the circular economy, and contribute to broader national and global sustainability objectives.
Currently, Bosch Limited is focused on four key areas under EPR:
Plastic packaging
Battery waste
Electronic waste (E-waste)
Oil waste management
Our first step is to develop 
reverse-logistics systems across all feasible segments. Products that have reached end-of-life will be collected, sorted, and directed into reuse, remanufacturing, or recycling streams. Our goal is zero waste to landfill, in alignment with our circular-economy vision.
This initiative depends on close 
collaboration with partners across our value chain, establishing a shared framework that benefits both business and the environment.

Complying with Due Diligence Obligations 
Relating to Human Rights and the Environment
As a globally operating company, we recognize our corporate responsibility to respect human rights. We contribute 
to improving human rights conditions worldwide by implementing due diligence obligations concerning human rights in our operational processes. At the same time, we actively demand respect for human rights in our global supply chains as well and take appropriate remedial measures in the case of violations.

100,000 under its CSR framework in the automotive value chain.Assessment and 
Monitoring
We regularly audit our suppliers both 
preventively and when the situation demands. Such an audit is generally carried out when we commence new supplier relationships, with the findings of our risk analyses then determining the type, scope, and frequency of the audits. Different methods are used depending on the prevailing framework conditions and the specific risk situation: verifications performed by Bosch itself (quick scans and drill-deep assessments), third-party audits, and self-declarations by suppliers.  Led by Purchasing, these 
three-year-valid reviews 
covered environmental

Supply-Chain Management
Compliance with human rights and 
environment-related requirements, such as those set out in our Codes of Conduct for Business Partners, already plays a crucial role when selecting new suppliers and is a prerequisite for subsequently entering into a contractual relationship. The corresponding timing and the audit methodology used are determined by the respective purchasing organizations according to the risk. As part of the sanctioned party list screening, a check is additionally carried out prior to the conclusion of a contract to determine whether potential business partners are included in sanction lists or affected by embargo regulations. 
If there is reasonable suspicion or 
concrete evidence of a violation of human rights or environment-related obligations by a supplier, we systematically investigate the facts of the matter. If we discover breaches of duty, we work to ensure that these are rectified immediately. Should this not be possible in the foreseeable future, we expect the supplier to present a plan and a specific time schedule for ending the breach and minimizing its effects. We track and monitor implementation of the measures – also by consistently requesting documented proof or by performing reassessments on site. Active suppliers found to be engaged in unlawful conduct or whose sustainability performance is deemed inadequate, such as a lack of effort in dealing with human rights or environment-related requirements, may be excluded by Bosch from any further awarding of contracts. If a supplier does not appear willing to fulfill our requirements or introduce corresponding measures, Bosch reserves the right to terminate the contractual relationship in extreme cases.
If there is reasonable suspicion 
of misconduct on the part of an indirect supplier, we initiate targeted preventive measures within the scope of our possibilities, such as controls and, if necessary, appropriate remedial measures through our business partners.

Building a Culture

Compliance refers to the 
observance of legal requirements and internal regulations. The global compliance management system (CMS) is an integral element of the measures for implementing corporate governance in the Bosch Group and comprises structures and processes for ensuring compliance at an organizational level. It is based on auditing standard IDW PS 980 and is described in an internal regulation. 
In addition to rule-based 
compliance, we are continuing to develop the values-based approach. Our ambition is that our associates not only regard values-based conduct as an obligation, but that they act in a compliant manner of their own volition. The CMS is preventive in nature and is designed to encourage all associates in the Bosch Group to identify compliance risks and violations at an early stage and to respond appropriately. This should also ensure a reduction in risks for the Bosch Group, its associates, and its corporate bodies. At the same time, we want to protect and cultivate the reputation of the Bosch Group, which is the basis of our customers’ and business partners’ trust. 
At Bosch Limited, the Compliance 
Officer is responsible for reporting protected disclosures and investigation outcomes regularly to the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors.
Codes of Conduct
In 2024, Bosch Group completely revised our Code of Business Conduct and republished it as the Code of Conduct. In addition to legal developments, the results of benchmarking studies and user expectations were also taken into account.  
The new document provides 
guidance for all Bosch associates on values-based, ethical, and legally irreproachable conduct. The Code of Conduct defines basic rules of conduct in the company and provides guidance on issues such as accepting gratuities or eliminating conflicts of interest. The Code of Conduct also describes our social responsibility, including respecting human rights. The basic principles of the Code of Conduct are specified in other central policies and in local regulations, in which we also take a clear stance against dumping. 
We feel that responsible and lawful 
conduct is important beyond company boundaries and have clearly formulated our expectations in our Code of Conduct for Business Partners. In this way we require suppliers to the Bosch Group to comply with human rights and environment-related principles and to put in place appropriate due diligence processes. We likewise require them to pass on this expectation to their own suppliers. Referenced in the Terms and Conditions of Purchase, this code is generally made an integral contractual element and is sent to all suppliers at the beginning of the business relationship.

Reporting Systems
Where potential misconduct is 
suspected within the Bosch Group or at suppliers, associates, and business partners as well as other third parties can make a disclosure via the Bosch Group’s reporting system. Our indoor environment sensors, including the BME690, detect volatile organic compounds and harmful gases, enabling users to maintain healthier indoor air quality.
appropriate IT tool, by e-mail, or phone.
Bosch’s reporting system and its 
reporting points support a number of languages. Associates and customers are actively made aware of the possibility of submitting a report. We also ask our suppliers to make their associates aware of the Bosch reporting system and to inform them accordingly. The objective is to make it as easy as possible for all target groups to submit reports and to ensure the widest possible accessibility. All reports are processed independently, impartially, autonomously, carefully, and confidentially. The principle of objectivity and the protection of whistleblowers are our top priority. Our rules of procedure set out the details of the different channels and principles, as well as the processing procedure.

Skill 
Development
Skill development remains 
a key pillar of Bosch India’s social engagement strategy. Our commitment is centered on equipping individuals, especially from underserved and marginalized communities, with the capabilities they need to thrive in an evolving job market. With a focus on employability and long-term economic independence, our programs are designed to bridge the skills gap through practical, inclusive, and purpose-driven learning.
Beyond technical training, we 
emphasize the importance of essential life skills that prepare beneficiaries for a wide range of career paths. Whether someone is entering the workforce for the first time or seeking to advance their career, our programs provide the tools, knowledge, and support necessary for meaningful progress.
Spanning sectors such as 
automotive services, healthcare, employability skills, and service-based vocations, our training approach is both comprehensive and future-focused. We place strong emphasis on community participation and industry collaboration to ensure real-world relevance and sustainable outcomes. By aligning with national frameworks such as the National Skill Development Mission and prioritizing hands-on learning, Bosch India continues to contribute to building a skilled, confident, and competitive workforce for tomorrow’s economy.
BRIDGE: Creating 
Pathways to Employability
Launched over a decade ago, 
BRIDGE (Bosch’s Response to India’s Development and Growth through Employability Enhancement) is a flagship initiative focused on enhancing the employability of youth with limited formal education. The program is designed to equip underprivileged and unemployed individuals with practical, industry-relevant skills that prepare them for entry-level roles in the service sector.
BRIDGE blends classroom-based 
training in soft skills and life skills with structured on-the-job training (OJT), enabling participants to develop both workplace readiness and confidence. Since its inception, the program has empowered over 110,000 young people, providing them with genuine opportunities for economic advancement.
In 2024–25 alone, over 22,600 
youth were trained across 24 states and 4 union territories through a robust network of more than 400 training partner centers. Notably, 57% of the beneficiaries were women, and 68% of all trainees who completed the program by March 2025 were successfully placed in employment.
To scale its reach and strengthen 
institutional collaboration, Bosch has partnered with the Department of Industrial Training and Employment (DITE), Government of Karnataka, and the Department of Skill, Employment and Entrepreneurship (DSEE), Government of Rajasthan, to establish 20 BRIDGE skill centers within government-run Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs).

Water Conservation and Afforestation
Lake Rejuvenation: Restoring 
Life to Water BodiesBosch’s long-standing commitment 
to water conservation continues to yield tangible benefits for communities and ecosystems alike. The rejuvenation of Shanumangala Lake and later Sheshagirihalli Lake in Bidadi, Karnataka, was a fundamental part of our efforts, transforming a neglected water body into a productive rainwater harvesting site. The initiative improved water retention by desilting, enhanced green cover along the shoreline, and restored biodiversity while protecting the lake from encroachment. In 2024–25, we started rejuvenation work in Mailsandra Lake in Bengaluru and Nathanallur Melandai Thangal Lake in Chennai.
Expanding Water Conservation 
through Targeted Projects
In addition to lake rejuvenation, 
Bosch implemented region-specific water conservation projects in 2024–25. The ridge-to-valley watershed restoration project in Nashik was launched to improve groundwater recharge and control soil erosion. Simultaneously, we undertook the rejuvenation of percolation tanks in Nashik and pond restoration in Jaipur to enhance localized water management systems. These interventions are expected to benefit 9,781 community members, providing them with more reliable access to water resources. Together, they contribute to the creation of sustainable water infrastructure that strengthens climate resilience and supports agricultural productivity in water-stressed regions.
Over these past years 26 water 
conservation projects have collectively impacted 1,10,000 of individuals and cattle and conserving an estimated 3 billion liters of water. Each intervention strengthens environmental sustainability, supports biodiversity, and improves local water security for future generations.

The initiative reinforces our commitment to climate resilience, sustainable agriculture, and ecological restoration.

Building on the momentum of 2024–25, the organization will continue to expand programs across skill development, sustainable mobility, and integrated community development. Guided by the principle of ‘with 
the community, not for the community,’ every intervention will be participatory and co-created, ensuring that impact is both inclusive and enduring. Bosch will also place greater emphasis on employee volunteering by creating more avenues for associates to engage in high-impact social initiatives, further fostering a culture of giving and collective responsibility. Through these continued efforts, Bosch remains committed to creating shared value for people, communities, and the planet.

22. Pursuant to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/ CMD/
CIR/P/2020/242 dated December 09, 2020, under 
Regulation 44 of Securities and Exchange Board of India 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, listed entities are required to 
provide remote E-voting facility to its shareholders, in 
respect of all shareholders’ resolutions. However, it 
has been observed that the participation by the public 
non-institutional shareholders/retail shareholders is at 
a negligible level. Currently, there are multiple E-voting 
service providers (ESPs) providing E-voting facility to 
listed entities in India. This necessitates registration 
on various ESPs and maintenance of multiple user 
IDs and passwords by the shareholders. To increase 
the efficiency of the voting process, pursuant to a 
public consultation, it has been decided to enable 
E-voting to all the demat account holders, by way of a 
single login credential, through their demat accounts/
web sites of Depositories/Depository Participants. 
Demat account holders would be able to cast their 
vote without having to register again with the E-voting 
service providers, thereby, not only facilitating 
seamless authentication but also enhancing ease 
and convenience of participating in E-voting process. 
Individual shareholders holding securities in demat 
mode are allowed to vote through their demat 
account maintained with Depositories and Depository 
Participants. Shareholders are advised to update their mobile number and email Id in their demat accounts to 
access E-voting facility.
23. The resolutions as set out in this Notice are being 
conducted through E-voting. The said resolutions will 
not be decided by show of hands at the AGM. The 
members can opt for only one mode of voting i.e., 
either by remote E-voting or by electronic ballot at the 
meeting. The members who have cast their vote by 
remote E-voting are eligible to attend the AGM but shall 
not be entitled to cast their vote again. In case of any 
unforeseen technical failure or eventuality resulting 
into non- functionality of the electronic voting system 
at the meeting, members would be provided the ballot 
paper for casting their vote at the meeting.

interchangeably.

ITEM No. 11
It is proposed to provide loan to the Companies (“Borrowing Companies”) mentioned in the resolution in which the Directors 
of the Company are Directors.
Section 185 of the Companies Act, 2013 prohibits giving of loan to any person in whom any of the Directors of the Company is 
interested which includes any Private Company of which any Director of the Company is a Director or Member.
Section 185 of the Companies Act, 2013 further provides that a Company may advance any loan including any loan represented 
by a book debt, or give any guarantee or provide any security in connection with any loan taken by any person in whom any of 
the Director of the Company is interested subject to compliance with the following conditions:
1. Approval of the Members of the Company is obtained by the Company for giving the loan and
2. The loans are utilized by the borrowing Companies for its principal business activities.
The above restriction is not applicable to any loan given by the Company to its wholly owned subsidiary company or any 
guarantee given, or security provided by the Company to its wholly owned subsidiary company provided that the loans given 
are utilized by the Subsidiary Company for its principal business activities.
The names of the Directors of the Company who are Directors of the Companies mentioned in the resolution are given below:
Sr. No Name of the Director Name of the Company
1. Mr. Guruprasad Mudlapur Bosch Global Software Technologies Private Limited
2. Mr. Guruprasad Mudlapur Bosch Chassis Systems India Private Limited
3. Mr. Guruprasad Mudlapur Bosch Automotive Electronics India Private Limited
4. Mr. Sandeep Nelamangala ETAS Automotive India Private Limited
5. Ms. Karin Gilges (CFO and Alternate Director) Prebo Automotive Private Limited

in which directors of the Company are interested, for a period of 5 years from December 12, 2020, to December 11, 2025.
Considering the growing business of these Companies (as mentioned above), it is proposed to provide financial support to 
these Companies vide group company loan which holds surplus cash or any loan represented by book debt or give guarantee 
or provide any security in connection with any loan taken by any of the borrowing Companies in whom any of the directors of 
the Company are interested up to an amount not exceeding ` 1500 Crores in aggregate. Instead of borrowing from an external 
financial counterparty, it is preferable to use the surplus cash available to fund the group companies at arm’s length pricing. 
Hence, the Company is intending to further provide loans for a further period of 5 years from December 12, 2025.The loan 
including any loan represented by a book debt or guarantee given or security provided in connection with any loan taken by any 
of the borrowing Companies in whom any of the directors of the Company are interested shall be used by these Companies for 
their principal business activities only.
The terms and conditions for the loan including any loan represented by a book debt or guarantee given or security provided in 
connection with any loan taken by any of the Borrowing Companies in whom any of the directors of the Company are interested 
shall be on arm’s length basis and the loans shall be secured by the Corporate Guarantee of Robert Bosch GmbH, the Holding 
Company.

Economic Scenario
Macroeconomy in 2024:
Global growth was unsynchronized across the developed, 
emerging /developing economies in the year 2024, where 
US saw its growth projections for 2024 being revised 
upwards, due to strong private demand in the US, outpacing 
expectations. On the other hand, Eurozone countries, 
UK and China saw slower-than-expected growth, though 
inflationary impulses came down as well. Consumer 
demand was muted, and the export powerhouse of 
Europe saw a slowdown in overall demand. Overall, the 
US economy emerged as the key driver of global growth 
among developed markets, also getting the moniker of “US 
exceptionalism.”
India, though logging in another year of positive growth 
and the “fastest growing economy tag,” also experienced 
a moderate slowdown compared to the previous years due 
to higher base impact with private capex not gathering the 
necessary momentum.
Global Economy
Global growth expectations are unraveling – in the US, 
due to trade issues and in other developed countries due 
to uncertainty. Global growth is projected to drop to 2.8% 
in 2025 and 3.0% in 2026 (down from 3.3% for both years 
from the earlier forecast) and much below the historical 
average of 3.7% (2000–2019). 
Growth in advanced economies is projected to be lower at 
1.4% in 2025 (Actual 2024: 1.8%), on account of increased 
policy uncertainty, trade tensions, geo-political risks, and 
softer demand momentum. In emerging and developing 
economies, growth is expected to slow down to 3.7% in 
2025 and 3.9% in 2026 (Actual 2024: 4.3%), with significant 
downgrades for countries affected most by recent trade 
measures from the US, such as China. 
Global headline inflation is expected to decline, albeit at 
a slower pace than what was expected initially, reaching 
4.3% in 2025 and 3.6% in 2026, with notable upward 
revisions for advanced economies and slight downward 
revisions for emerging market and developing economies 
in 2025. This also leads to projections of stagflation 
impulses in few developed economies. This is intensifying 
the downside risks that dominate the economic outlook, 
amidst escalating trade tensions and financial market 
adjustments.

On the upside, a de-escalation from current tariff rates and 
new bilateral trade agreements may provide clarity and 
stability in trade policies that could lift global growth. Due 
to the soft growth projections, oil prices are also showing 
signs of correction, which could impact inflation positively.
Indian Economy
The uncertainties in the global economy may weigh on 
India’s growth this year. However, India is relatively more 
stable due to dependence on the domestic market and 
expected to grow at 6.2% in 2025-26 and 6.3% in 2026-
27 (Provisional Actual: 6.5% in 2024-25), supported by 
domestic private consumption, particularly in rural areas, 
but this is 0.3% points lower than the earlier forecast 
due to escalating levels of trade tensions and global geo-
political uncertainties. The recent domestic conflicts with 
the neighboring country may also add to the uncertainties. 
However, the central bank, RBI is expected to cut interest 
rates further, to support growth.
Amidst the gloomy outlook, the latest IMF forecasts provide 
a positive take on India, which is set to overtake Japan as the 
world’s 4th largest economy in 2025. As per latest projection 
by IMF, India will remain the fastest growing major economy 
over the next 2 to 3 years.
Industry Structure and Development 
Automotive
Indian Automotive Industry 2024-25: Resilient Growth 
Amid Geo-Political Headwinds
Despite entering 2024-25 with a high base from the 
previous fiscal year and contending with global economic 
uncertainties and India’s general elections, the Indian 
automotive industry demonstrated resilience and 
adaptability, delivering a varied performance across 
segments, with 4-wheeler production reaching a new high 
of 7.2 million units in 2024-25, surpassing the previous peak 
of 7.0 million units in 2023-24.
Passenger car sales grew 3.6% Y-on-Y, due to strong SUV 
demand, despite weak small/hatchback car performance 
and high inventory levels. 2-wheelers showed 11.2% 
increase Y-on-Y, driven by domestic demand, export 
recovery, and rising EV adoption. 3-wheeler sales rose 
by 7.1% owing to growing e-commerce and last-mile 
connectivity. Tractors bounced back with 7.7% growth 
Y-on-Y, supported by good monsoon and rural investments 
after a 11.7% drop in the previous year. Meanwhile, light 
commercial vehicles declined by 5.1% due to competition 
from electric 3-wheelers, and heavy commercial vehicles 
fell by 1.3% due to a high base and delays in execution of 
infrastructure projects.
In 2024-25, the electric vehicle (EV) market grew across all 
segments. Electric 2-wheelers witnessed biggest growth 
due to strong urban demand and low operating costs. Also 
3-wheelers grew on account of increase in demand for 
delivery vehicles. Electric buses faced some delays but are 
expected to grow with government support. The growth of EV charging infrastructure and government incentives 
helped to boost adoption.
Overall, the industry reflected a shift towards electrification 
and rural-driven recovery. Vehicle production (excluding 
2-wheelers) registered a 3.5% Y-on-Y growth, reflecting the 
sector’s ability to navigate structural shifts and evolving 
market dynamics.
Vehicle segment wise performance in 2024-25:
• Heavy Commercial Vehicle (HCV): Market shift 
dampens growth, but Buses rebound.
 The Heavy Commercial Vehicle (HCV) segment 
reported a 1.3% Y-on-Y decline in production, primarily 
attributed to the high base effect from 2023-24 and 
disruptions arising from the general elections, which 
slowed infrastructure project execution. Projects 
started gradually getting rolled out in the second 
half of 2024-25. Furthermore, there is a shift towards 
higher-tonnage vehicles, driven by infrastructure 
development, supportive government initiatives, 
and rising demand for cargo transport. Moreover, 
the bus sub-segment rebounded well, marking a 
return in public transportation investments and fleet 
replacements by state undertakings and private 
operators.
• Light Commercial Vehicle (LCV): E 3-Wheelers 
disrupt traditional LCV space.
 Light Commercial Vehicle (LCV) production declined 
by 5.1% Y-on-Y, due to increasing competition from 
the rapid adoption of electric 3-wheelers (E-3Ws), 
particularly in the sub-2-tonne category. Small 
commercial vehicles (SCVs) are also moving toward 
higher payload pickups, prioritizing efficiency, and 
productivity.
 E-3Ws have emerged as the preferred choice for urban 
e-commerce deliveries and last-mile connectivity, 
prompting traditional LCV players to revisit their 
product strategies and value propositions. However, 
rural demand regained momentum in the post-
monsoon months, providing a boost to LCV volume 
offtake towards the latter part of the fiscal.
• Passenger Car (PC): UV demand drives growth 
amid inventory challenges
 Passenger car (PC) segment reached an all-time high 
production of 5.1 million units in 2024-25, marking a 
shift from ‘recovery’ to ‘growth’, continuing to rise 
steadily due to the consistent demand for Utility 
Vehicles (UVs).
 Mid-year inventory levels became a concern, peaking 
to 70 days in September, owing to sluggish movement 
in small and hatchback segments. However, the 
situation improved significantly towards the fiscal 
year-end, with inventory days stabilizing around 50–55 
days, indicating a recovery in consumer sentiment and 
demand traction.
154
=== page 158 ===
• 3-Wheelers: Electrification and E-Commerce 
push segment forward
 3-wheelers grew by 7.1% Y-on-Y, driven by higher 
demand for passenger transport and the fast-growing 
e-commerce sector. Moreover, rising use of electric 
3-wheelers in food delivery, logistics, and urban 
transport services contributed to the growth of this 
segment.
 The segment’s evolution continues to reflect a broader 
structural shift toward clean mobility solutions and 
cost-effective last-mile delivery options. E-3Ws are 
gaining market share from CNG models.
• Tractors: Monsoon and rural investments spur 
late-year recovery
 After a slow start in the first half of 2024-25, the tractor 
segment made a remarkable comeback, ending the 
year with an 7.7% Y-on-Y growth. The rebound was 
supported by a favorable monsoon, hiked Minimum 
Support Prices (MSPs), and stepped-up rural 
infrastructure spending. Though, early headwinds such as election-related 
disruptions and patchy rainfall muted sentiments, the 
sector regained its footing as improved agri-economics 
and rural policy support revitalized demand in the 
second half of the fiscal year.
• 2-Wheeler (2W): Rural revival and premium 
demand fuel double-digit growth
 The 2W segment emerged as a star performer in 
2024-25, registering a robust 11.2% Y-on-Y growth. The 
recovery was powered by improved rural demand, and 
a surge in urban replacement demand, especially for 
premium models.
 Electric 2-wheelers also gained traction, contributing 
to the segment’s overall growth despite challenges like 
reduced subsidies and high input costs.
 Moreover, the revised income tax slabs introduced in 
the Union Budget are expected to boost disposable 
income, further sustaining positive growth momentum 
into the upcoming fiscal year.

Non-Automotive
Power Tools
India’s robust economic expansion, infrastructure development and manufacturing growth are key macroeconomic factors 
fueling the power tools market. Rising GDP growth, increased government spending on infrastructure projects (Bharat Mala, 
Sagarmala, Urban development) and policy initiatives like ‘Make in India’ and the PLI scheme have boosted construction, real 
estate, and industrial activities. Additionally, growing FDI inflows, urbanization, rise of domestic manufacturing and restrictions 
on low-quality imports further supports in making India a high-growth region for power tools.
The Indian power tools market is currently valued at approximately 110 billion INR and is projected to grow at 7.0% in the coming 
year. The market is witnessing increased competition, particularly from new entrants - primarily Chinese manufacturers - who 
are gaining traction in the mid-price segment, thereby challenging established players. However, the Indian government has 
implemented measures to regulate imports, including stricter BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) certification requirements 
for imported products and restrictions on license renewals, aiming to curb dependency on foreign suppliers and support 
domestic industry growth.
Building Technologies
The building technologies business sector which consists of Safety and Security systems is witnessing consistent growth 
across various segments in Indian economy. This expansion is driven by the country’s focus on infrastructure development and 
a surge in construction activities, supported by substantial investments in areas like transportation, energy, manufacturing,

Strategic Employee Relations (ER) Framework: 
Enhancing Business Competitive Advantage
At Bosch, Employee Relations (ER) is more than a 
function, it is a strategic enabler driving business 
excellence. Our Employee Relations Framework is 
designed to create a future-ready, compliant, and 
collaborative  ecosystem that goes beyond managing 
Industrial Relations reactively. It builds a resilient 
foundation that anticipates challenges and embraces 
continuous improvement.
The Employee Relations is guided by a well-defined 
framework built on seven strategic pillars , each 
playing a critical role in shaping a future-ready, 
resilient, and high-performing.
ER ecosystem.
The first pillar, Assessment , focuses on conducting 
holistic and comprehensive maturity assessments of 
the ER function at both location and enterprise levels. 
These assessments help identify gaps, promote best 
practices, and enable structured action planning and 
execution of all the ER processes. 
162
=== page 166 ===
The second pillar, Engagement , emphasizes structured and sustainable interaction with both internal and external 
stakeholders. Through initiatives like engagement calendars, GPTW surveys, participative committees, and stakeholder 
connect programs, Bosch encourages an environment of transparency, trust, and continuous feedback. This initiative-
taking engagement helps align workforce aspirations with organizational goals.
Capability Building , the third pillar, aims to strengthen ER competencies across all layers of the organization. At Bosch, 
we believe that effective Employee Relations are built through consistent investment in people and capabilities. In line 
with this philosophy, Bosch ERA (Employee Relations Academy)  was launched in 2024 as a structured, scalable, and 
future-focused initiative aimed at building ER competencies across all levels of the organization. With the guiding mantra 
of “Learn. Adapt. Transform,”  Bosch ERA goes beyond conventional training to create a strategic platform that nurtures 
a culture of empathy, compliance, and collaborative growth. 
Bosch ERA engages a wide spectrum of stakeholders 
including HR teams, front-line managers, union 
leaders, and departmental heads through a 
thoughtfully curated curriculum covering topics like 
contract labor management, grievance handling, 
labor laws, and conflict resolution, etc. Delivered via 
a blended learning approach  that combines web-
based modules, classroom sessions, real-life case 
studies, and cross-functional projects, Bosch ERA has 
already trained over 550 participants in its first year.
The fourth pillar, Conflict Resolution , promotes 
a transparent, collaborative, and human-centric 
approach for resolving workplace issues. Grievance 
handling procedures, structured playbooks, and 
enabling supervisors to manage concerns effectively 
are key elements that support early intervention and 
uphold employee trust.The fifth pillar, Compliance , highlights Bosch’s 
commitment to maintaining initiative-taking and 
robust legal adherence. With mechanisms like internal 
audits, digital compliance monitoring, vendor audits, 
etc., we ensure that all processes operate within the 
regulatory framework.
Sustainability , the sixth pillar, aims to build a 
balanced ER ecosystem capable of supporting long-
term business goals. It includes transformation of 
labor models, harmonization of ER documentation 
and policies, and structured risk assessments to 
help the organization anticipate and navigate future 
challenges effectively.
Finally, the seventh pillar, Governance , provides a 
participatory structure that reinforces communication, 
accountability, and trust. By implementing clear 
policies and frameworks, conducting periodic reviews, 
and promoting collaborative ER governance, Bosch 
ensures consistency and ownership across all levels.
